questions.q: Radius of the circle $(x+5)^2+(y-3)^2=36$ is
questions.solution:
Comparing the equation of the circle $(x+5)^2+(y-3)^2=36$
with $(x-h)^2+(y-k)^2=r^2\therefore \quad-h=5$ or $h=-5, k=3, r^2=36 \Rightarrow r=6\therefore \quad$ Centre of the circle is $(-5,3)$ and radius $=6$

questions.q: If the tangent at the point $P$ on the circle $x^2+y^2+2 x+2 y=7$ meets the straight line $3 x-4 y=15$ at the point $Q$ on the $X$-axis, then length of $P Q$ is
questions.solution:
$\because Q$ is on the $X$-axis.
Let, the coordinates of $Q=(h, 0)$ Then, $(h, 0)$ lies on the line.
Therefore, $3 h-4 \times 0=15 \Rightarrow h=5$
That means, coordinates of $Q=(5,0)$
We know, the length of tangent $=\sqrt{S_1}$ and $S_1=(5)^2+(0)^2+2 \times 5+2 \times 0-7=35-7=28$
Hence, the length of $P Q=\sqrt{28}=2 \sqrt{7}$

questions.q: The equation of one of the common tangents to the parabola $y^{2}=8 x$ and $x^{2}+y^{2}-12 x+4=0$ is
questions.solution:
Any tangent to parabola $y^{2}=8 x$ is $y=$
\mathrm{mx}+\frac{2}{\mathrm{~m}}......(i)

It touches the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}-12 x+4=0$ if the length of perpendicular from the centre $(6,0)$ is equal to radius $\sqrt{32}$.
$\begin{array}{l}
\therefore \frac{6 \mathrm{~m}+\frac{2}{\mathrm{~m}}}{\sqrt{\mathrm{m}^{2}+1}}=\pm \sqrt{32} \\
\Rightarrow\left(3 \mathrm{~m}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{~m}}\right)^{2}=8\left(\mathrm{~m}^{2}+1\right) \\
\Rightarrow\left(3 \mathrm{~m}^{2}+1\right)^{2}=8\left(\mathrm{~m}^{4}+\mathrm{m}^{2}\right) \\
\Rightarrow \mathrm{m}^{4}-2 \mathrm{~m}^{2}+1=0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{m}=\pm 1
\end{array}$
Hence, the required tangents are $y=x+2$ and $y=-x-2$.

questions.q: Two common tangents to the circle \(x^2+y^2=2 a^2\) and parabola \(y^2=8 a x\) are
questions.solution:
Any tangent to the parabola \(y^2=8 a x\) is
\(y=m x+\frac{2 a}{m}\) ...(i)
If(i) is a tangent to the circle, \(x^2+y^2=2 a^2\) then,
\(\begin{aligned}
& \sqrt{2} a= \pm \frac{2 a}{m \sqrt{m^2+1}} \\
\Rightarrow & m^2\left(1+m^2\right)=2 \Rightarrow\left(m^2+2\right)\left(m^2-1\right)=0 ; \Rightarrow m \\
= & \pm 1 .
\end{aligned}\)
So from (i), \(y= \pm(x+2 a)\).

questions.q: If two different circles $x^2+y^2+2 a x+2 b y+1=0$ and $x^2+y^2+2 b x+2 a y+1=0$ touches each other, then $(a+b)^2$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$x^2+y^2+2 a x+2 b y+1=0$
Center $\left(c_1\right)=(-a,-b)$
Radius $\left(r_1\right)=\sqrt{a^2+b^2-1}$
and $x^2+y^2+2 b x+2 a y+1=0$
Center $\left(c_2\right)=\left(-b_1-a\right)$
Radius $\left(r_2\right)=\sqrt{a^2+b^2-1}\because$ Both circle touches each other.
$\begin{aligned}
& \text { So, } C_1 C_2=r_1+r_2 \\
& \Rightarrow \sqrt{(-a+b)^2+(-b+a)^2}=\sqrt{a^2+b^2-1} \\
& +\sqrt{a^2+b^2-1} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \sqrt{2(a-b)^2}=2 \sqrt{a^2+b^2-1} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 2\left(a^2+b^2-2 a b\right)=4\left(a^2+b^2-1\right) \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 2 a^2+2 b^2-4 a b=4 a^2+4 b^2-4 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 2 a^2+2 b^2+4 a b=4 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 2(a+b)^2=4 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad(a+b)^2=2
\end{aligned}$

The diameter of the circle is perpendicular distance between the parallel lines (tangents) $3 x-4 y+4=0$ and

questions.q: The tangent at $(1,7)$ to the curve $x^{2}=y-6$ touches the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}+16 x+12 y+c=0$ at
questions.solution:
The tangent at $(1,7)$ to the curve $\mathrm{x}^{2}=\mathrm{y}-6$ is

\begin{array}{l}
x=\frac{1}{2}(y+7)-6 \\
\Rightarrow 2 x=y+7-12 \\
\Rightarrow y=2 x+5
\end{array}

which is also tangent to the circle
$x^{2}+y^{2}+16 x+12 y+c=0$
i.e. $x^{2}+(2 x+5)^{2}+16 x+12(2 x+5)+c=0\Rightarrow 5 x^{2}+60 x+85+c=0$, which must have equal roots.
Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of the equation.
Then $\alpha+\beta=-12 \Rightarrow \alpha=-6(\because \alpha=\beta)\therefore x=-6, y=2 x+5=-7\therefore$ Point of contact is $(-6,-7)$.

questions.q:
The value of $x$, for which the matrix
$A=\left[\begin{array}{ccc}\frac{2}{x} & -1 & 2 \\ 1 & x & 2 x^{2} \\ 1 & \frac{1}{x} & 2\end{array}\right]$ is singular, is
questions.solution: We know that, A is singular if $|\mathrm{A}|=0|\mathrm{A}|=\left|\begin{array}{llc}\frac{2}{\mathrm{x}} & -1 & 2 \\ 1 & \mathrm{x} & 2 \mathrm{x}^{2} \\ 1 & \frac{1}{\mathrm{x}} & 2\end{array}\right|=0\Rightarrow|\mathrm{A}|=\frac{2}{\mathrm{x}}[2 \mathrm{x}-2 \mathrm{x}]+1\left[2-2 \mathrm{x}^{2}\right]+2\left[\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}}-\mathrm{x}\right]=0\Rightarrow \frac{2}{\mathrm{x}}[0]+\left[2-2 \mathrm{x}^{2}\right]+\frac{2}{\mathrm{x}}-2 \mathrm{x}=0\Rightarrow 2 \mathrm{x}-2 \mathrm{x}^{3}+2-2 \mathrm{x}^{2}=0\Rightarrow \mathrm{x}^{3}+\mathrm{x}^{2}-\mathrm{x}-1=0\Rightarrow \mathrm{x}^{2}(\mathrm{x}+1)-1(\mathrm{x}+1)=0\Rightarrow(\mathrm{x}+1)\left(\mathrm{x}^{2}-1\right)=0\Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=\pm 1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A manufacturer of cotter pins knows that $5 \%$ of his product is defective. He sells pins in boxes of 100 and guarantees that not more than one pin will be defective in a box. In order to find the probability that a box will fail to meet the guaranteed quality, the probability distribution one has to employ is
questions.solution:
Poisson distribution is a probability distribution which is obtained when the probability (p) of the happening of an event is same in all the trials and there are only two events in each trials generally says successes and failures probability (p) of the happening of the event in trial is very less but number of trials $(\mathrm{n})$ is very large.
Here, $\mathrm{p}=5 \%=\frac{5}{100}=\frac{1}{20}$ is very less and $\mathrm{n}=100$, is very large. Hence, one has to employ the Poisson distribution in the given question.

questions.q: The number of real roots of the equation $\left(x+\frac{1}{x}\right)^{3}+x+\frac{1}{x}=0$ is
questions.solution:
$\begin{array}{l}
\left(x+\frac{1}{x}\right)^{3}+\left(x+\frac{1}{x}\right)=0 \\
\Rightarrow\left(x+\frac{1}{x}\right)+\left[\left(x+\frac{1}{x}\right)^{2}+1\right]=0 \\
\Rightarrow x+\frac{1}{x}=0 \Rightarrow x^{2}+1=0 \Rightarrow x=\pm i
\end{array}$
Thus, the given equation has no real roots.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The maximum value of $\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}}\right)^{\mathrm{x}}$ is
questions.solution:
Let $\mathrm{y}=\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}}\right)^{\mathrm{x}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{y}=\mathrm{x}^{-\mathrm{x}}$
Then $\log y=-x \log x\therefore \frac{1}{y} \frac{d y}{d x}=-(1+\log x)$
or $\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}=-\mathrm{y}(1+\log \mathrm{x})\& \frac{\mathrm{d}^{2} \mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{dx}^{2}}=-\mathrm{y} \cdot \frac{1}{\mathrm{x}}-(1+\log \mathrm{x}) \cdot \frac{\mathrm{d} \mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{dx}}\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{d}^{2} \mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{dx}^{2}}=-\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}}\right)^{\mathrm{x}+1}-(1+\log \mathrm{x}) \cdot \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}$
Now, $\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}=0 \Rightarrow 1+\log \mathrm{x}=0\Rightarrow \log x=-1=-\log \mathrm{e}=\log \left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}}\right)\Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}}\right)$
Also, $\frac{\mathrm{d}^{2} \mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{dx}^{2}}$ at $\mathrm{x}=\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}}\right)$ is $-\mathrm{e}^{1+\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}}} \lt  0\left[\because \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}=0\right]$
So, $x=\left(\frac{1}{e}\right)$ is a point of local maxima.
$\therefore$ Maximum value
$=\left(\right.$ value of $\mathrm{y}$ when $\left.\mathrm{x}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}}\right)=\mathrm{e}^{\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The two curves $y=3^{x}$ and $y=5^{x}$ intersect at an angle
questions.solution:
Given curves are $y=3^{x}$ ...(i)
and $y=5^{x}$ ...(ii)
intersect at the point $(0,1)$
Now, differentiating eqs. (i) and (ii) w.r.t. $x$, we get

\begin{array}{l}
\frac{d y}{d x}=3^{x} \log 3 \text { and } \frac{d y}{d x}=5^{x} \log 5 \\
\Rightarrow\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)_{(0,1)}=\log 3 \text { and }\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)_{(0,1)}=\log 5 \\
\Rightarrow m_{1}=\log 3 \text { and } m_{2}=\log 5
\end{array}

Angle between these curves is given by

\begin{array}{l}
\tan \theta=\frac{m_{1}-m_{2}}{1+m_{1} m_{2}} \\
\Rightarrow \tan \theta=\frac{\log 3-\log 5}{1+\log 3 \cdot \log 5} \\
\Rightarrow \theta=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{\log 3-\log 5}{1+\log 3 \log 5}\right)
\end{array}
